claims.claim: DOJ filed a civil Sherman Act Sections 1 and 2 suit against Visa on September 24, 2024 in S.D.N.Y. over debit network markets.
claims.quote: The Justice Department filed a civil antitrust lawsuit today against Visa for monopolization and other unlawful conduct in debit network markets
claims.title: Justice Department Sues Visa for Monopolizing Debit Markets
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Fetched via web.archive.org copy of the justice.gov page (Akamai blocks direct curl); page carries 'Updated February 6, 2025'.

claims.claim: DOJ says Visa carries more than 60% of U.S. debit transactions and charges over $7 billion a year in fees on them.
claims.quote: more than 60% of debit transactions in the United States run on Visa's debit network, allowing it to charge over $7 billion in fees
claims.title: Justice Department Sues Visa for Monopolizing Debit Markets
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same press release later says 'roughly $8 billion in network fees on U.S. debit volume annually'; see contradictions.

claims.claim: DOJ alleges Visa's agreements with merchants and banks penalize customers that route to another debit network or alternative payment system.
claims.quote: These agreements penalize Visa's customers who route transactions to a different debit network or alternative payment system.
claims.title: Justice Department Sues Visa for Monopolizing Debit Markets
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: DOJ alleges Visa pays would-be competitors to become partners rather than enter as debit competitors.
claims.quote: Visa also induces would-be competitors to become partners instead of entering the market as competitors by offering generous monetary incentives
claims.title: Justice Department Sues Visa for Monopolizing Debit Markets
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa's merchant and acquirer volume commitments use cliff pricing so any shortfall triggers rack rates on all Visa transactions.
claims.quote: Visa insists on cliff pricing to discourage merchants from routing to Visa's competitors, denying them scale.
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 78; PDF fetched via web.archive.org copy and read with pypdf (71 pages).

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa holds de facto exclusive routing contracts with more than 180 of its largest merchants and acquirers.
claims.quote: has now entered de facto exclusive routing contracts with over 180 of its largest merchants and acquirers
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 98.

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa's merchant/acquirer contracts cover over 75% of Visa debit volume and foreclose at least 45% of total U.S. debit volume.
claims.quote: cover over 75% of Visa's debit volume and results in the foreclosure of at least 45% of total U.S. debit volume
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 98.

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa's issuer contracts incentivize issuers to disable or not enable card-present PINless, making more transactions non-contestable.
claims.quote: Visa uses its contracts with issuers to incentivize the issuers to make decisions—like choosing to disable card-present PINless
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 98; para. 106 quotes a Visa executive fearing a large issuer enabling CP PINless could 'create a tipping point'.

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa, as dominant front-of-card network, can process all transactions on over 70% of U.S. debit card payment volume.
claims.quote: By virtue of being the dominant front-of-card network, Visa is enabled to process all transactions on over 70% of debit card payment volume
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 92.

claims.claim: The complaint says non-Visa/Mastercard debit networks collectively hold about 11% of all debit transactions and about 5% of card-not-present debit.
claims.quote: the non-Visa/Mastercard-owned networks collectively represent only about 11% of all debit transactions and only about 5% of card-not-present debit transactions
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 20; para. 6 says Mastercard is 'a distant second, processing less than 25%'.

claims.claim: The complaint names STAR, NYCE and Pulse as examples of unaffiliated back-of-card networks alongside Visa's Interlink and Mastercard's Maestro.
claims.quote: Examples of such unaffiliated back-of-card networks include Mastercard's Maestro or a smaller debit network such as STAR, NYCE, or Pulse.
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 41. Predates Capital One's May 18, 2025 acquisition of Discover/PULSE.

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa's agreements with Apple, PayPal and Square turned potential debit competitors into partners.
claims.quote: Visa's agreements with these companies, including Apple, PayPal, and Square, have succeeded in transforming these potential competitors into partners
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 21.

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa used threatened wallet fees and rack rates to push PayPal into an expansive routing contract and away from ACH.
claims.quote: used the threat of exorbitant wallet fees and high rack rates on these Visa transactions to induce PayPal
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 122.

claims.claim: The complaint alleges Visa contracted with Square for Square Cash because it feared Square would otherwise build an ACH option.
claims.quote: Visa worried that if it did not sign a contract for Square Cash, Square was "likely to build in an ACH option."
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 127; para. 126 alleges the Square contracts 'foreclosed Square from competing aggressively against Visa'.

claims.claim: The complaint quotes Visa's former CFO on its partner-not-competitor strategy toward wallets, big tech and large merchants.
claims.quote: [E]verybody is a friend and partner. Nobody is a competitor.
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 110.

claims.claim: DOJ pleads two relevant markets: general purpose debit network services and general purpose card-not-present debit network services, with monopolization and attempted monopolization counts.
claims.quote: Visa has monopolized, in violation of Section 2 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. § 2, two relevant markets
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 182; para. 188 pleads attempted monopolization of the same two markets; para. 156 includes fintech debit networks in the market.

claims.claim: The complaint says Visa charges over $7 billion in U.S. debit network fees annually, earning $5.6 billion net revenue, its largest revenue source globally.
claims.quote: Visa charges over $7 billion in network fees on U.S. debit volume annually, earning Visa $5.6 billion in net revenue.
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., No. 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Complaint para. 64.

claims.claim: Visa's FY2025 10-K discloses DOJ CIDs in 2021 and 2023 focused on U.S. debit and competition with other payment methods and networks.
claims.quote: The CIDs focused on U.S. debit and competition with other payment methods and networks.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.publisher: Visa Inc. via SEC EDGAR
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 10-K also records a 2012 CID on PIN-authenticated Visa Debit and the fixed acquirer network fee.

claims.claim: Visa's FY2025 10-K states the court denied Visa's motion to dismiss the DOJ complaint on June 23, 2025.
claims.quote: On June 23, 2025, the court denied a motion to dismiss filed by Visa.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.publisher: Visa Inc. via SEC EDGAR
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 10-K summarizes the complaint as alleging monopolization 'through agreements with merchants, acquirers, and others'.

claims.claim: Judge Koeltl's June 23, 2025 memorandum opinion denied Visa's Rule 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss (ECF 37).
claims.quote: For the foregoing reasons, Visa's motion to dismiss the complaint is denied.
